newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch see Samsung talks on Fokker rescue Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Dutch see Samsung talks on Fokker rescue Wednesday.

text.p: Talks aimed at a rescue package for bankrupt Dutch planemaker Fokker NV will begin on Wednesday between South Korea's Samsung Aerospace, the Dutch government and Fokker's receivers, Dutch Economic Affairs Minister Hans Wijers said on Tuesday.
"Talks will start tomorrow," Wijers told Dutch television. "I've learnt not to be over-optimistic about this (Fokker re-start). It's all very difficult."
The Dutch parliament earlier gave Wijers the go-ahead to start negotiations with Samsung and Fokker's court-appointed receivers.
Samsung handed its Fokker business plan to the Dutch government last week, asking The Hague to take a minority stake in a new Fokker and pump in large subsidies.
Samsung is seeking around 600 million guilders in Dutch state subsidies, via share capital, loans, and re-start costs, plus cash to develop a new 125- or 130-seater aircraft.

Fokker was declared bankrupt in March, after majority shareholder Daimler Benz Aerospace withdrew a crucial cash lifeline, saying it was no longer prepared to carry the aviation pioneer's huge losses.
Fokker has since been kept alive artificially by court-appointed receivers.
